Sophie (AE): Quick heads-up — ACME is pushing an MFN + 12-month price-protection clause that would retro-adjust prices if we lower list. They want a $500k commit + 25% discount floor. Need legal + deal desk input asap.
Anna (Sales): Yikes. MFN + retroactivity is basically open-ended exposure. Do we have a playbook? :thinking: 
Raj (Deal Desk): We saw a variant of this last year. Legal removed the retroactive piece and we capped exposure. If accepted as-is, downside could be material depending on future list changes.
Mike (Legal): Can you paste the exact language they redlined?
Sophie (AE): They sent this snippet:
```
Customer shall receive Most-Favored-Nation treatment such that if Provider offers any third party or other customer a lower price for the same service during the Term, Provider shall adjust Customer's price retroactively to such lower price for the entire Term.
```
Mike (Legal): :grimacing: That wording is too broad. Major issues: (1) retroactivity for the entire Term; (2) no carve-outs for promos/launches/marketplace; (3) no cap on exposure. We should counter.
Raj (Deal Desk): Quick back-of-envelope: with product launches and occasional promotional pricing, the worst-case credit could reach 20-30% of the committed revenue in a year. With reasonable carve-outs and a short retro window the impact drops to single digits.
Jules (CFO): We need explicit numeric scenarios before we agree to anything. Also prefer a hard-dollar cap (or % of ARR) on total price protection exposure. Open-ended credits are a no-go.
Anna (Sales): From customer POV, they want protection if we drop list for a new model family. Could we limit MFN to 'materially equivalent SKUs/models' and same commercial region? That would narrow it.
Mike (Legal): Agreed. Proposed counter elements: MFN applies only to published list prices for materially equivalent services; exclude promotional/limited-time offers and marketplace/channel partner pricing; cap retroactivity to 90 days; add a maximum credit equal to 10% of the customer's annual committed spend; include audit and notice windows.
Raj (Deal Desk): 10% cap seems reasonable. For a $500k commit that'd be $50k max credit — workable from a deal-desk risk budget. We can absorb that as a concession if it helps close.
Jules (CFO): If we do a % cap, also tie it to the committed spend calculation and require the customer to notify us before invoking MFN remedies. And add a sunset: MFN expires on renewal unless re-negotiated.
Sophie (AE): I'll propose the counter language to the buyer. Can Legal draft the redline with the 90-day retro + 10% cap + promo carve-outs? I need something to present tomorrow.
Mike (Legal): Will draft a counter and circulate by EOD. I'll include language variants (tight vs. moderate) so we can choose based on negotiation levers.
Anna (Sales): Also ask them to limit MFN to 'commercially material price changes' — e.g., changes that alter per-token/per-embed unit price by >5%. That prevents tiny list tweaks triggering credits.
Raj (Deal Desk): Good idea. Also recommend excluding partner/channel and marketplace offers.
security-bot: FYI — security questionnaire for ACME (POC) submitted. Expected turnaround 48-72h.
Sophie (AE): Thanks — flagging POC security timeline to the buyer. Next steps: Mike drafts, Raj confirms numeric impact, I present counter tomorrow morning. I'll loop back once we have the redline.
Anna (Sales): :thumbsup:
Mike (Legal): Draft in flight. Will add the audit right and notification windows Jules requested.
Sophie (AE): Great — appreciate the fast turnaround.
